title: The storehouse
hook: the storehouse consciousness where the seeds of habit are kept (Lankavatara)

segments.voice: Yesterday, a finger pointed at the moon, and the trick was to look past it. Your line: not the finger. Where did you catch yourself staring at the words instead? Day one thousand one hundred ninety-eight.

Why do the same words come out in the same argument, year after year? Nobody sits down at the kitchen table and decides to say them again. They're just there, ready, before anyone has thought anything at all. The Lankavatara Sutra, and the Yogacara teachers who worked with the same ideas, gave a name to the place where that readiness waits, out of sight, between one moment and the next. Today: the storehouse.
screen: `THE SAME WORDS, THE SAME FIGHT.` → `READY BEFORE ANY THOUGHT.` → `WHERE DOES IT WAIT?`

segments.voice: The name is alaya-vijnana, usually translated storehouse consciousness. Yogacara teachers described the mind in layers. On top, the ones everyone knows: seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the thinking mind that sorts it all out. Under those, a layer that quietly keeps insisting there's a fixed self in charge. And beneath everything, the storehouse. What's kept there? Seeds. That's the word these teachers used. Every action, every word, every thought leaves a seed behind in the storehouse. The seed sits there, unseen. Then one day the conditions are right, a certain tone of voice, a certain tired evening, and the seed ripens. Out comes the reaction, fully formed, as if from nowhere. And that ripening plants new seeds of its own. That's how a habit keeps itself going. The Lankavatara has a picture for this: the storehouse is like the ocean, and the other kinds of consciousness are like waves, stirred up by the wind of what we see and hear. The waves and the ocean are not two separate things. Buddhist schools have argued about this idea. Some worried that a storehouse sounds too much like a hidden, permanent self. Yogacara teachers answered that it's a stream, never the same from one moment to the next, more like a river than a box. The same teaching runs the other way. Seeds can be planted on purpose. A kind word leaves a seed too. So does a pause, a breath before answering, one honest apology. Those seeds also wait in the dark, and they also ripen, sometimes long after anyone remembers planting them.
screen: `A STOREHOUSE UNDER THE MIND.` · `EVERY ACT LEAVES A SEED.` · `AN OCEAN AND ITS WAVES.` · `SEEDS PLANTED ON PURPOSE.` · then, large: `SEEDS IN THE STOREHOUSE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: plant one good seed. Settle, and let the breath find its own pace. Notice how many reactions come up on their own as you sit: an itch, a plan, a little worry. Those are seeds ripening. Let them pass. Then choose one small good thing you could do today. A thank-you. A slower reply. Holding a door. Picture yourself doing it, simply, once. Let the intention sink down, like a seed pressed into soil. You don't have to watch it grow. The bell holds the time.
The storehouse. Alaya-vijnana, the deep layer of mind where, Yogacara teaches, the seeds of every action wait to ripen. Today's word.
Your line: seeds in the storehouse. Today, when an old reaction ripens, notice it, and plant one different seed right after. Day one thousand one hundred ninety-eight.

howItsDone: In Yogacara study, and in East Asian and Tibetan schools that inherited it, the storehouse consciousness and its seeds are taught as a way to understand how habits and karma carry forward from moment to moment.

fork.setup: you're a Yogacara teacher, and a student says the storehouse sounds like a hidden, permanent self. what do you answer?
options: it doesn't matter what it is.
fork.reveal: Yogacara teachers answered that the storehouse is a stream, more like a river than a box, never the same from moment to moment.

original.note: Sanskrit: the storehouse consciousness. ālaya, a dwelling or store; vijñāna, consciousness.

trapdoor: what you thought: the subconscious, under another name.
what it means: a deep layer of mind where every action leaves a seed that ripens later, keeping habits going.
what a scholar hears: alaya-vijnana, central to Yogacara; the Lankavatara pictures it as an ocean with the other consciousnesses as its waves.

sources.ref: Lankavatara Sutra, the ocean-and-waves passage on the alaya-vijnana
Yogacara teaching on seeds (bija) and the storehouse consciousness

notes: All paraphrase. The layered model (five sense consciousnesses, thinking mind, self-clinging mind, storehouse) is described without giving the count of eight; confirm the description.
Seeds (bija) as a Yogacara term; the Lankavatara speaks more of habit-energies (vasana). Confirm the hook's 'the Lankavatara Sutra, and the Yogacara teachers who worked with the same ideas' framing.
Ocean-and-waves image with 'wind of objects' paraphrased from the Lankavatara; confirm.

'Buddhist schools have argued about this idea; some worried it sounds like a permanent self' — fair summary of Madhyamaka and other critiques and the Yogacara reply (stream, like a river, cf. Trimsika's 'flowing like a torrent'); confirm wording.
Original note gives the parts of the compound (ālaya, vijñāna); confirm.
Editor pass: replaced the 'quiet good news' uplift line with a plain turn.
